summary: ESLint config downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload at install
details: @ornikar/eslint-config-react@24.0.4 declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is variable-name-obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style `_0xXXXX` identifiers, string-object indirection) and, when Bun is not already on PATH, downloads the Bun runtime tarball from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against the shipped math_init.js — a 727KB heavily obfuscated `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle using a rotating string-array decoder. An ESLint configuration package has no legitimate need to fetch a separate JavaScript runtime at install time to execute a bundled opaque payload; running the payload under a freshly installed alternate runtime bypasses Node-based inspection, and the payload itself is unreadable without executing it. This matches the alternate-runtime-dropper install-time RCE pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
